title: Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation for stem wilt resistance in asparagus
author: Helong Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.68bhhsn
materials: DNA Extraction and confirmation of transformation Newly growing embryos were placed in a seedling culture medium to become seedlings. The seedlings were transplanted to the prepared nutrition substrate after induction, and the asparagus seedlings were managed and held for detection. The kit method was adopted to extract transgenic asparagus seedling DNA. The P2 primer mentioned in vector construction was used for PCR verification. Moreover, integration of the hevein-like gene was further confirmed by southern blot hybridization. Genomic DNA of T1 generation transgenic plant leaves was used as template, genomic DNA of non-transgenic plant leaves was used as negative control, and plasmid pCAMBIA3300-35S-hevein-like-NOS DNA was used as positive control. Genomic DNA was digested overnight at 37°C using EcoR I and Hind III，separated by 0.8% agarose gel electrophoresis and transferred onto a Hybond-N membrane (Pharmacia, USA). The membrane was hybridized with the hevein-like-CDS DNA probe, which was random primed, labeled with Digoxigenin-11-dUTP using DIG-High Prime (Roche). Hybridization (at 42°C) and detection were performed following the instruction manual of the DIG High Prime DNA Labeling and Detection Starter Kit I (Roche, USA).

steps.title: Determine PPT Resistance Threshold
steps.instruction: Evaluate the survival rate of asparagus embryos across different glufosinate (PPT) concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Place 20 units of 0.6 cm² asparagus embryo blocks into transformation media with 0, 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80 mg/l PPT.
Record the survival rate after 20 days.
Extract and purify pBI121 and hevein-like carrying plasmids using manufacturer's kits.
Digest with Xba I and Sac I enzymes and perform gel extraction using an OMEGA kit.
Use P1 primers (F: 5′ TGCTCTAGAATGAAATACTGTACTATGTTTAT 3′; R: 5′ CGAGCTCTCAGTTGGCACCGC 3′) to add Xba I and Sac I cleavage sites to the hevein-like target gene.
Construct the pCAMBIA3300-35S-hevein-like-NOS vector following the same steps as pBI121-hevein-like.
Verify construction using P2 primers (F: CCCAAGCTTCATGGAGTCAAAGATTCAAATAG; R: GGAATTCCCCGATCTAGTAACATAGATGAC).

steps.title: Preculture Asparagus Embryos
steps.instruction: Preculture embryos in specific medium for 2 days at 26 °C under light.

substeps.instruction: Prepare preculture medium: MS culture medium, 4% sucrose, 800 mg/l Gln, 500 mg/l acid-hydrolyzed casein, 0.70 mg/l ancymidol, 0.10 mg/l NAA, and 0.50 mg/l kinetin (pH 5.8).
Place 0.6 cm² asparagus embryos in the medium.

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium Solution
steps.instruction: Cultivate Agrobacterium tumefaciens containing the pCAMBIA3300-35S-hevein-like-NOS plasmid.

substeps.instruction: Apply 20 μL of Agrobacterium onto YEP solid medium containing 50 mg/l Kanamycin and 100 mg/l Rifampin.
Incubate the medium upside down for 30 min, then cultivate at 28 °C for 2 days.
Inoculate a single colony into YEP fluid medium containing 50 mg/l Kanamycin and 100 mg/l Rifampin.
Shake cultivate at 250 rpm at 28 °C.
Centrifuge at 5500 rpm for 8 min when OD600 is approximately 0.55.
Use the resulting liquid transformation medium for suspension culture.

steps.title: Inoculate Embryos
steps.instruction: Inoculate precultured embryos with Agrobacterium solutions of varying concentrations and Acetosyringone (AS) levels.

substeps.instruction: Adjust the light absorption (OD600) of the bacterium solution to 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8.
Place cultivated embryos in a pasteurized 150 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Infiltrate embryos using 50 mL Acetosyringone (AS) liquid media of different concentrations (0, 50, 100, and 200 μmol/l) for durations of 5, 10, 20, and 40 min.
Shake cultivate at 26 °C at 150 rpm.

steps.title: Co-culture Embryos
steps.instruction: Co-culture the inoculated embryos on solid medium.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the invaded embryos dry.
Transfer to solid medium for dark culturing at 26 °C for 2, 4, 6, and 8 days.

steps.title: Remove Bacteria and Select Transformed Embryos
steps.instruction: Eliminate Agrobacterium and select for transgenic embryos using PPT.

substeps.instruction: Treat co-cultured embryos with 200 mg/l Timentin for 10 min at 100 rpm oscillation.
Wash embryos with distilled water and wipe dry.
Transfer to solid transformation medium containing glufosinate (PPT) and Timentin.
Culture under light at 26 °C and observe growth.
Perform the test in triplicate using 80 embryos per repeat to calculate the transformation percentage.

steps.title: Identify Disease Resistance
steps.instruction: Evaluate the stem wilt resistance of transgenic plants using the virulent strain BT05.

substeps.instruction: Prepare BT05 bacterial suspensions at 10^6/mL.
Spray the suspension onto three transgenic plants and three non-transgenic control plants of the same age (perform three replicates).
Maintain samples under high humidity for 48 hours, then remove plastic cover and allow natural infection at 25 °C to 28 °C.
On the 8th day post-inoculation, determine the disease level (Grade 0-4) based on the percentage of canopy area affected.
Calculate the Disease Index (DI) using the formula: DI = ∑ (plant number of disease grades × disease level value) / (number of total plants per replicate × 4) × 100.
